title: Mock 1 · Foundations
blurb: Core definitions across all 12 chapters: savings vs investment, PMS service types, exit loads and the basics of return.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes savings from investment?
options: Savings and investment are the same thing
Savings is income minus spending; investment is committing savings for a period expecting a higher amount
Investment is income minus spending; savings is committing money to stocks
Savings always involves real assets while investment involves only bank deposits
questions.explanation: The workbook defines savings as the difference between money earned and money spent, and investment as the current commitment of savings with an expectation of receiving a higher amount.
hints: Wrong: the workbook stresses they are not the same.
Correct: matches the workbook definitions.
Wrong: the definitions are reversed.
Wrong: savers use short-term liquid deposits; investors commit to real and capital market assets.

questions.q: A retired investor wants her portfolio to generate regular money through dividends, interest and rent to meet living expenses. Her investment objective is:
questions.explanation: Current income is pursued by investors, mostly retired people, who want regular income rather than growth in portfolio value.
hints: Wrong: capital appreciation targets growth in value over time.
Wrong: tax saving is about reducing tax burden.
Correct: regular dividend, interest and rental income is the current income objective.
Wrong: speculation is not an investment objective.

questions.q: In which type of issue does the company receive no money because existing shareholders sell shares already allotted to them?
options: Further public offer of fresh shares
questions.explanation: In an OFS, existing shareholders sell shares; there is no fresh issuance, so share capital does not increase and proceeds go to the offerors.
hints: Wrong: a rights issue raises fresh capital from existing holders.
Wrong: fresh shares in an FPO bring money to the company.
Wrong: QIP is fresh capital raised from QIBs.
Correct: OFS proceeds go to the selling shareholders.

questions.q: Which type of risk in equity investing cannot be diversified away, though it can be hedged?
questions.explanation: Market risk affects all listed assets, is proxied by beta and cannot be diversified away, though it can be hedged.
hints: Correct: market (systematic) risk is non-diversifiable.
Wrong: company-specific risk is diversifiable.
Wrong: sector-specific risk is non-systematic and diversifiable.
Wrong: this is a company-specific factor, diversifiable.

questions.q: A share trades at ₹240 and its EPS is ₹12. What is its P/E ratio?
questions.explanation: P/E = Price / EPS = 240 / 12 = 20 times.
hints: Wrong: this is the EPS itself.
Wrong: this multiplies instead of dividing.
Wrong: this is EPS / Price (earnings yield).

questions.q: The Economy-Industry-Company (EIC) framework for stock selection is an example of:
questions.explanation: The EIC approach starts with the economy, narrows to industries, then companies: a top-down fundamental approach.
hints: Wrong: technical analysis studies price and volume patterns.
Correct: EIC is the top-down approach.
Wrong: bottom-up starts from the company.
Wrong: arbitrage exploits price differences between markets.

questions.q: When market interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds generally:
options: Rise only for zero coupon bonds
questions.explanation: Market interest rates and bond prices have an inverse relationship: when rates increase, bond prices decline.
hints: Wrong: that happens when rates fall.
Wrong: prices adjust to the new rates.
Wrong: zero coupon bonds fall the most when rates rise.
Correct: inverse relationship.

questions.q: Which party to an option contract has a right but no obligation?
questions.explanation: The option buyer has the right but not the obligation; the writer must honour the contract if exercised.
hints: Correct: the holder pays a premium for the right.
Wrong: the writer has the obligation.
Wrong: only the buyer has a pure right.
Wrong: the clearing corporation guarantees settlement; it is not the option holder.

questions.q: Hedge funds that use long-short strategies, leverage and derivatives are classified as:
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs employ complex trading strategies such as short selling, derivatives and leverage; hedge funds are the example.
hints: Wrong: Category I covers VC, angel, social venture and infrastructure funds.
Wrong: Category II covers PE, debt funds and fund of funds.
Correct: hedge funds are Category III.
Wrong: InvITs own infrastructure assets.

questions.q: Under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, a portfolio manager shall not accept from a client funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The portfolio manager shall not accept funds or securities worth less than fifty lakh rupees (subject to exemptions for accredited investors and co-investment PMs).
hints: Wrong: far below the regulatory minimum.
Wrong: the minimum is higher.
Wrong: ₹1 crore is the AIF minimum mentioned in the workbook.
Correct: ₹50 lakh.

questions.q: A portfolio manager who manages funds strictly as per the directions of the client, consulting the client for every transaction but executing the trades itself, offers:
questions.explanation: A non-discretionary PM manages funds as per client directions; what and when to buy/sell rests with the investor while the PM executes.
hints: Correct: execution by PM, decisions by client.
Wrong: discretionary PMs decide themselves.
Wrong: in advisory, the client also executes.
Wrong: not a service type described this way.

questions.q: If a client redeems his PMS portfolio in the second year of investment, the maximum exit load that can be charged is:
questions.explanation: Exit load caps: 3% in year 1, 2% in year 2, 1% in year 3, and none after three years.
hints: Wrong: 3% applies in the first year.
Correct: 2% in the second year.
Wrong: 1% applies in the third year.
Wrong: nil applies only after three years.

questions.q: When must the Disclosure Document be given to a prospective PMS client?
options: Within 30 days after signing the agreement
Only on the client's written request
Along with the account opening form, prior to signing the agreement
questions.explanation: Regulation requires the Disclosure Document to be given with the account opening form prior to signing the agreement, and it must also be on the PM's website.
hints: Wrong: it must come before signing.
Wrong: it is mandatory, not on request.
Correct: before the agreement is signed.
Wrong: far too late.

questions.q: Operating expenses (excluding brokerage) charged by a portfolio manager over and above the PMS fee shall not exceed:
options: 0.50% per annum of the client's average daily AUM
1% per annum of the client's average daily AUM
2.25% per annum of the client's year-end AUM
questions.explanation: Operating expenses excluding brokerage shall not exceed 0.50% per annum of the client's average daily AUM.
hints: Correct: 0.50% p.a. of average daily AUM.
Wrong: the cap is lower.
Wrong: wrong figure and wrong base.
Wrong: the regulation imposes a cap.

questions.q: A portfolio manager must report a suspicious transaction to FIU-IND within:
questions.explanation: The portfolio manager is required to report any suspicious transaction within 7 working days to FIU.
hints: Wrong: 24 hours is not the STR timeline.
Wrong: 21 days is the grievance redressal timeline.
Wrong: too long.
Correct: 7 working days.

questions.q: What is the first step in the portfolio management process?
questions.explanation: The first step is development of the Investment Policy Statement (IPS), a road map of risk appetite, objectives and constraints.
hints: Wrong: construction is the third step.
Correct: the IPS comes first.
Wrong: performance measurement is the last step.
Wrong: rebalancing is part of ongoing monitoring.

questions.q: A correlation coefficient of -1 between two assets means:
options: They move in exactly the same direction
There is no relationship between them
They move in exactly opposite directions
questions.explanation: Correlation ranges from -1 to +1; -1 is perfect negative correlation, meaning assets move in opposite directions.
hints: Wrong: that is +1.
Wrong: that is 0.
Correct: perfect negative correlation.
Wrong: correlation says nothing about being risk free.

questions.q: Which asset allocation approach maintains a long-term fixed mix (e.g., 70:30 equity-bond) and rebalances periodically?
questions.explanation: SAA sets fixed long-term proportions and rebalances periodically to restore them; the workbook's example is a 70:30 equity-bond portfolio maintained over decades.
hints: Wrong: TAA makes short-term active shifts.
Wrong: momentum is a style factor.
Wrong: market timing is the opposite of a fixed mix.
Correct: SAA.

questions.q: In risk profiling, an investor's financial ABILITY to take risk is called:
questions.explanation: The workbook lists risk tolerance as willingness to take risk and risk capacity as financial ability to take risk.
hints: Correct: capacity = ability.
Wrong: tolerance = willingness.
Wrong: liquidity need is access to funds.
Wrong: horizon is the timeframe for goals.

questions.q: A portfolio worth ₹10,00,000 at the start of the year is worth ₹11,50,000 at the end, and ₹50,000 of dividends were received. What is the holding period return?
hints: Wrong: ignores the dividend income.
Wrong: counts only the dividend.
Wrong: arithmetic slip.

questions.q: The Sharpe ratio measures excess return per unit of:
questions.explanation: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) / σp, i.e., reward to variability using total risk (standard deviation).
hints: Wrong: beta is used in the Treynor ratio.
Wrong: variance is SD squared; Sharpe uses SD.
Correct: standard deviation.
Wrong: risk-free rate is in the numerator.

questions.q: For a resident individual, listed equity shares held in a PMS qualify as long-term capital assets if held for more than:
questions.explanation: Equity shares and equity-oriented MFs are long-term if held for more than 12 months.
hints: Wrong: 24 months applies to debt investments.
Wrong: not the threshold in the workbook.
Wrong: too short.
Correct: more than 12 months.

questions.q: For an individual investor reporting PMS income as capital gains, management fees and performance fees paid to the portfolio manager are:
options: Not deductible while computing capital gains
questions.explanation: Management fees, brokerage, GST and performance fees are not deductible while computing capital gains tax for individuals.
hints: Wrong: they are not deductible.
Correct: no deduction allowed.
Wrong: no partial deduction exists.
Wrong: applies to both STCG and LTCG.

questions.q: Under PMLA, intermediaries must keep a record of all cash transactions of value more than:
questions.explanation: PMLA requires records of all cash transactions of value more than ₹10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency.
hints: Correct: more than ₹10 lakh.
Wrong: not the PMLA threshold.
Wrong: ₹50 lakh is the PMS minimum.
Wrong: too high.

questions.q: As per the code of conduct for PMS distributors, which of the following is a distributor NOT allowed to do?
options: Assist clients in KYC and in-person verification
Assure returns in an investment approach
questions.explanation: Distributors must abstain from assuring returns in any investment approach and from any misrepresentation.
hints: Wrong: assisting with KYC is required.
Wrong: disclosing commissions is required.
Correct: assuring returns is prohibited.
Wrong: confidentiality is required.
